patches.after: The three fundamental components of the finite element method for elliptic partial differential equations: variational formulation, Galerkin approximation, and Céa's lemma. All propositions are discussed on finite-dimensional subspaces, and a complete proof of Céa's lemma is given in Section 2.3. This material is self-written for offline demonstration, and citations and page numbers can be checked line by line against the pages of this lecture note. Keywords: variational problem; Galerkin approximation; Céa's lemma; V-ellipticity; a priori error estimates | Reading Tip: You can select any paragraph, ask a question in the right Research Agent, then click "Locate Original Text" to return to the corresponding paragraph on this page.
